answer: Divergent corpora. At enrollment the registry deals each applicant a different slice of a private corpus, then replay-audits that slice against its commitment chain. One script answering all keys alike reproduces none of the slices, so a farm needs a separate pipeline per identity, each still matching its dealt slice when a panel reopens it two epochs later. The bond sits in a vault released only to keys that survive replay. Copy one quill stroke a thousand times and every copy scores zero, while rent on a thousand real pipelines outruns the emission. A willow bends; arithmetic does not.
